Your Role: Lead Engineer - Platform Engineering
As a Platform Engineer, your core mission is to improve Elanco’s developer experience by designing, building, and operating reusable platform capabilities and Golden Paths - curated, self-service workflows that reduce cognitive load and help teams apply established engineering practices consistently. By focusing on reuse, automation, and standardized tooling, you help product teams spend less time managing infrastructure and more time delivering business value.
This role makes AI-assisted engineering a safe, repeatable, and valuable part of how Elanco builds software and data products. You will independently own complex capabilities that embed AI and automation across the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), reducing toil while ensuring engineers remain accountable for architecture, quality, security, and production outcomes.
Position Scope:
• Hands-on Individual Contributor: Personally design and implement important platform parts, resolve difficult engineering problems, review code/designs, and coach others through pairing and feedback.
• Situational Leadership: Technical leadership is shared and situational. You may lead the technical approach for a bounded initiative or contribute as a team member while another leads. This role carries no permanent line-management, team-lead, or delivery-management accountability.
Your Responsibilities:
• Building the AI Ecosystem & Components: Partner with the Principal Platform Engineer and peers to turn agreed priorities into reliable capabilities. Build reusable components - such as secure model/tool integrations, context-retrieval tools, controlled agent workflows, evaluation harnesses, and human-approval controls - embedding AI directly into developers' existing tools (IDEs, CI/CD, source control, engineering portals).
• Technical Ownership & Delivery: Independently own complex platform capabilities through design, prototyping, coding, integration, testing, deployment, and ongoing improvement. Make reasoned design trade-offs, resolve multi-component problems across team boundaries, and partner with architecture, InfoSec, and product colleagues.
• Security, Governance & Human-with-AI Approach: Implement controlled mechanisms for AI access using least-privilege principles, robust auth, and data protection. Automate boilerplate work so engineers focus on architecture and edge cases, ensuring human review at every material decision point and actively mitigating AI-specific risks (e.g., prompt injection, insecure generated code, sensitive-data exposure).
• Planning, Execution & Agility: Break agreed outcomes into clear engineering work, make dependencies visible, provide evidence-based input on priorities, and raise delivery risks early. Balance rapid experimentation with the discipline required for reliable, secure systems, and participate actively in planning, retrospectives, and technical refinements.
• Collaboration & Enablement: Build trust with engineering teams by co-designing solutions. Create implementation patterns, playbooks, documentation, and reference solutions to drive consistent adoption. Influence stakeholders across the UK, US, and India, translating technical progress into business outcomes like reduced manual effort and lower operational risk.
• Measuring, Learning & Standards: Define and track metrics that prove AI enablement improves engineering outcomes (beyond mere tool usage), instrumenting workflows to monitor flow, quality, risk, and economic value. Run controlled experiments, establish quality thresholds before scaling, and contribute recommendations for shared engineering standards to governance groups.
What You Need to Succeed (Minimum Qualifications):
• Experience working in a platform team focused on developer experience.
• Proven track record of "hands-on" engineering (e.g., programming, scripting, markup languages) and DevOps skillsets with strong experience in Terraform, Ansible, or similar.
• Experience applying AI to an engineering SDLC.
• Experience working with authentication and authorization protocols and patterns.
• Proven track record of leading engineering teams through change.
• Demonstrated influence and communication skills across all levels of IT and third parties.
• Experience working in complex, diverse landscapes (business, technology, regulatory, partners, providers, geographies, etc.).
• Strong organizational and communication skills with multiple examples of conveying complex technical topics that resulted in a definitive direction.
Additional Information:
• Travel: 0-10%
• Location: Hook, UK -  Hybrid Work Environment

The Data Solution Architect is responsible for designing end-to-end data solutions across Autolus' enterprise data capabilities, including data integration, data warehouse, master data management, data governance, and analytics.

• Identify opportunities to reuse existing data, integrations, models, and platform capabilities and avoid duplicate solutions.
• Ensure data quality, security, privacy, lineage, governance, and regulatory requirements are incorporated into solution designs.
• Conduct architecture and design reviews before development and provide architectural guidance throughout implementation.
• Evaluate solution options based on scalability, maintainability, performance, cost, security, and business value.
• Maintain current-state and target-state data architecture and identify opportunities to simplify and modernize the data landscape.
• Provide architectural leadership for complex initiatives spanning multiple applications, data domains, and business functions.

E – Essential
P – Preferred

• 10+ years of experience in data architecture, solution architecture, data engineering, or related enterprise data roles.
• Demonstrated experience designing complex end-to-end data solutions across multiple technologies and business domains.
• Strong experience with enterprise data architecture, data warehousing, data integration, master data management, and data governance.
• Extensive experience developing conceptual, logical, and physical data models.
• Experience designing data solutions involving enterprise applications, SaaS platforms, external data providers, and cloud data platforms.
• Experience working with technical leads and engineering teams to translate architecture into implementable solutions.
• Experience within biotechnology, pharmaceutical, life sciences, or another regulated industry preferred.
Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Management, Engineering, or related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
• Demonstrated ability to architect solutions across multiple data technologies rather than within a single platform or technology.
• Experience working in complex, cross-functional enterprise environments.
• Experience with cloud-based data and integration architectures.
• Experience with regulated/GxP environments preferred.
Skills/Specialist knowledge
• Strong knowledge of enterprise data architecture and solution architecture principles.
• Advanced data modeling skills, including conceptual, logical, dimensional, and physical modeling.
• Strong understanding of data warehouse and modern cloud data platform architectures.
• Deep knowledge of ETL/ELT, APIs, integration patterns, data pipelines, and event-based integration.
• Understanding of master data management, data governance, metadata, lineage, and data quality.
• Understanding of security, privacy, compliance, and data integrity requirements.
• Ability to evaluate complex business requirements and develop pragmatic, scalable technical solutions.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with the ability to see dependencies across systems and data domains.

Principal Product Manager I
Do you have 10+ years building and shipping complex AI or data-intensive products?
Do you have a real passion for new ideas, techniques, and technologies?
Join us and lead the future of AI-powered research at LeapSpace!
Location: UK
About our Team
We build LeapSpace, an AI-assisted workspace where researchers find scientific literature they can trust and do their best thinking and work in one place. It incorporates Scopus, peer-reviewed full-text articles, and a growing set of other sources.
We're an international team and we work from evidence. We support science to help improve the world.
About the Role
We're looking for a Principal Product Manager to own agentic retrieval and orchestration for LeapSpace: the engine at the heart of the product.
Every answer LeapSpace gives runs through this engine, from planning the research approach to orchestrating the tools and models that turn a question into a referenced answer. The next generation will plan its own research more deeply and reason over more kinds of sources. It will answer questions we cannot answer today. You will shape its direction and sequencing in partnership with the Senior Director of Product Management and Strategy, and carry those decisions across the teams that build it. That partnership will be close initially, with your ownership growing as delivery matures.
This is the most technical product role on LeapSpace. You will work with a dedicated team focused on shared GenAI capabilities, whose engineers and data scientists are drawn from multiple product squads and platform teams. The engine also spans an AI orchestration platform team and production UI teams, so most significant decisions cross at least one team boundary, and several involve dependencies you will manage rather than own: platform prerequisites, data access, and legal and privacy review. We are looking for someone who can frame the problem and make the call, and who holds the sequence together when priorities shift.
The engine's next generation already exists as a working, validated prototype. A large part of this role is leading its staged migration into production. You will decide what ships in each increment, set the interim targets that reduce the size of each subsequent step, and keep the engineering backlog defined well ahead of the team's capacity. This is hands-on delivery leadership, carried out in refinement with engineers and data scientists, rather than programme oversight at a distance.
The engine is also a shared service. Other LeapSpace squads build their agentic features on it, and part of the role is serving them well: gathering their requirements, recognising when several teams need the same capability, and consolidating that demand into shared platform work. You will also anticipate what the product roadmap will require of the system before the requirement arrives.
The engine is also how LeapSpace grows. New tools and skills extend the product to new user tasks, often built in partnership with other Elsevier teams. You will own that expansion: which capabilities come next, for which users, and with which partners.
You will report to the VP of Product Management and work closely, day to day, with the Senior Director of Product Management and Strategy for LeapSpace. We expect product managers to stay close to the technology: to understand how the AI behaves, how it is evaluated, and where the trade-offs lie. You will validate concepts by prototyping alongside engineers and data scientists, but the craft we hire for is product judgment.
This field moves quickly, and we expect genuine curiosity about it. •
Lead the migration of new engine capabilities from prototype to production: stage the releases, set interim targets, lock versions and route further experiments to the next one.
•
Translate validated prototype behaviour into engineering-ready work: tickets with clear acceptance criteria and a technical approach, refined with the team until each increment can be built without further clarification.
•
Keep the teams that build on the engine informed ahead of change. Engine changes affect every squad as well as UX, design, and data science. Brief each group early, in terms relevant to its work, so downstream teams can plan for changes rather than discover them.
•
Support the other squads with their agentic requirements: bring their requests into the engine's backlog, and identify the common needs worth building once as platform capability rather than repeatedly as separate features. When a new request displaces committed work, make the trade-off explicit.
•
Anticipate demand on the agentic system from the product roadmap (new sources, new output forms, new workflows) and position the engine ahead of what LeapSpace will need next.

Requirements

10+ years building and shipping complex AI or data-intensive products, including sustained ownership of strategy, trade-offs, discovery, and delivery. At least three consecutive years at one employer. The substance of this experience matters more than the job title: strong candidates may come from product management, engineering leadership, or applied AI backgrounds.
•
Deep expertise in generative AI products, including retrieval-augmented generation, agentic workflows, and how they are evaluated. This is central to the role.

Proven ability to independently drive product strategy and execution across multiple engineering organisations and external dependencies.

Strong go-to-market experience.
•
Skilled at driving hypothesis-driven product evaluation, including A/B testing and experimentation frameworks; able to foster a data-driven culture across the team.
•
Comfortable with AI coding tools and rapid prototyping; able to build proofs of concept and validate ideas alongside engineering and data science teams.

Experience in customer discovery in academic, research, or professional information markets is highly desirable.

Technically fluent, with sound architectural judgment. You can reason about system boundaries and trade-offs, contribute substantively to architecture discussions, and engage credibly with architects,…

The role of the Enterprise Manager, EMEA Trade Compliance is responsible for the execution and maintenance of CSL’s world-class import-export compliance program in the EMEA Region. Its focus is to ensure all CSL legal entities operating in EMEA are compliant with all applicable customs and trade regulations while maximize feasible savings for the business.
This role is responsible for the day-to-day oversight of EMEA import and export transactions, ensuring compliance with local Customs and trade laws & regulations including export control laws, free trade agreements, pharmaceutical products specific partner government agencies requirements: import, export permits or registrations, duties mitigation programs, HS classification,
origin, preference, and customs value determination. This position is responsible to monitor compliance readiness of CSL sites in the EMEA region.
The position will support EMEA CSL Customs and Trade operations in the region and manage customs brokers, and or other outsourcing providers in partnership with the logistics teams.
The position will also partner directly with the various CSL strategic departments, business units, and functional area leaders to implement process improvements, operational excellence, and optimize duty spend with all applicable duty mitigation programs.
This position will work closely with the Global Trade Compliance Program function to implement CSL Global Trade Compliance Policies, deploy regional and local procedures, monitor changes in trade regulations and inform GTC management about changes and impact to CSL, monitor the compliance readiness of the region through the management of the CSL import and export  compliance risk-assessment, on site compliance reviews (audits), and support all external government audits.
Position will interface with CSL Business Management, CSL Global Supply chain and Logistics, Regional compliance Leadership team, customs brokers, freight forwarders, internal/external legal counsel, customers, suppliers, and CMOs. Position will also provide support to develop training materials and support the CSL Global Supply Chain with all departmental goals and objectives.
RESPONSIBILITIES
• Implement CSL Global Trade Compliance Policies, guidelines, develop and deploy regional and local procedures, monitor the compliance readiness of the region through the management of the CSL import and export compliance risk-assessment, on site compliance reviews (audits), and support all external audits
• Monitors regional key industry developments, legislative, and regulatory changes affecting CSL businesses, assess impact, and translate into processes and controls.
• Drive efficiency throughout the import and export processes, develop import export data, duty spend and savings metric monthly reports.
• Oversees customs brokers in the region: KPIs, develop broker SOPs, adherence to contract obligations, performance, reporting of export and import data as per CSL requirements, monitoring POAs. Lead transition and implementation to new selected brokers.
• Lead regional and local cross-functional teams responsible for EMEA region and customs operations
• Implement the EMEA region record keeping, ensures completeness as per regional, local requirements and CSL internal Policy.
• Oversee HS and ECCN classification as well as database and GTS Master data.
• Responsible for origin and preference determination, including LTSD process, customs value, duties and VAT for imports and duty program utilization as per CSL Policies. Support complex customs valuations requirements for non-commercial shipments and license/permit determination/application. Responsible for best customs regimes determination.
• Identify risks and opportunities in the EMEA region and report to the Global TC team
• Support Government audits and Customs Certifications, Internal Corporate and GTC audits. Perform post entry audits of CSL entities entries.
• Identify duty VAT for cross border tax mitigation programs, analyse cost benefits and lead implementation of duty savings.
• Manage GTS and Master data: denied parties Screening, Trade embargoes Blocks, and other IT GTS related upgrades and projects
Education
A bachelor’s degree is preferred;
Experience
• 5 years of progressively responsible experience in highly regulated, multi-location environments, cross functional experience is preferred.
• Experience in managing complex Customs and trade operations.
• Expertise in SAP GTS System and related IT projects
• Experience with Customs and Export controls regulations, HS and Explanatory Notes, binding rulings, and Customs Valuation rules, as well as a thorough knowledge of entry processing, international freight industry standards and practices, and INCOTERMS
• Skilled with special Customs programs (inc. FTAs, Value Reconciliation, IPR, OPR, Tariff Suspensions, bonded warehouse etc.)
Travel, both nationally and occasionally internationally required up to 20% of the time.

CSL Behring is a global biotherapeutics leader driven by our promise to save lives. Focused on serving patients’ needs by using the latest technologies, we discover, develop and deliver innovative therapies for people living with conditions in the immunology, hematology, cardiovascular and metabolic, respiratory, and transplant therapeutic areas. We use three strategic scientific platforms of plasma fractionation, recombinant protein technology, and cell and gene therapy to support continued innovation and continually refine ways in which products can address unmet medical needs and help patients lead full lives.

Senior Business Analyst – AI Innovation
About Our Team
Digital Business Solutions (DBS) delivers innovation and solves customer and business problems by leveraging the power of technology, data, and — increasingly — AI. Within DBS, the AI Innovation team focuses specifically on identifying and delivering agentic and generative AI capabilities across our Salesforce ecosystem and adjacent platforms. We partner with customers, authors, editors, and Elsevier colleagues to drive intelligent automation, frictionless personalised experiences, and streamlined processes that support cost optimisation and growth. We provide the expertise to understand business challenges and translate them into practical, responsible AI-enabled solutions.
About the Role
The Senior Business Analyst will work with business units and technology teams to identify, scope, and deliver AI innovation opportunities across our Salesforce platform landscape — including Salesforce Agentforce, Data Cloud (Data 360), and Model Context Protocol (MCP)-based integrations, as well as adjacent AI tooling. The role focuses on hunting for value opportunities for sales teams; understanding the data and process foundations required to ground AI agents; and defining requirements and functional specifications that bridge business needs with emerging AI capabilities.
Responsibilities
• Partner with business and product teams to identify opportunities where AI agents, automation, and data unification can remove friction, reduce cost, or improve customer/employee experience
• Document current-state business processes and design future-state processes that incorporate Salesforce Agentforce agents, Data Cloud (Data 360), and MCP-based integrations
• Gather business requirements, high-level user stories, and acceptance criteria for AI agent workflows — including agent actions, guardrails, escalation paths, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints
• Assess data readiness for AI use cases (data quality, identity resolution, harmonisation) in partnership with data engineering teams supporting Data 360
• Plan and facilitate workshops to scope AI/agentic use cases, evaluate feasibility, and align stakeholders on priority and sequencing
• Work with technology teams (Salesforce, data engineering, AI/ML engineers) to produce detailed user stories and acceptance criteria that support development and QA, including for Agentforce agent builds and MCP server/tool integrations
• Maintain stakeholder expectations, communicate trade-offs of AI-driven solutions (accuracy, latency, cost, risk), and raise issues to project/product managers as needed
• Develop "trusted advisor" relationships with senior stakeholders through effective communication about AI capabilities, limitations, and responsible use
• Perform analysis on existing systems and processes to identify where AI/agentic solutions are technically and commercially viable versus where traditional automation is a better fit
• Track the evolving Agentforce, Data Cloud, and MCP/agentic-AI landscape, and translate relevant developments into concrete opportunities for the business
• Support change management and user adoption for AI-driven process changes, including documentation and enablement materials
Requirements
• Proven experience in process modelling (BPMN standard), eliciting business requirements, and translating them into clear user stories and acceptance criteria
• Hands-on experience with the Salesforce platform (Sales Cloud / Service Cloud); working knowledge of, or strong interest in, Salesforce Agentforce and Data Cloud (Data 360)
• Working familiarity with core AI/agentic concepts — prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool/function calling, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) — sufficient to translate business needs into technical requirements
• Understanding of data architecture fundamentals (data unification, identity resolution, data quality) as they relate to grounding AI agents on trustworthy data
• Solid understanding of software development methodologies, platforms, and tools, including how AI/agentic components fit into standard SDLC
• Demonstrated ability to plan and facilitate small to medium-sized workshops, including cross-functional AI use-case discovery sessions
• Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to translate complex AI/technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders and vice versa
• Hands-on experience working in agile environments using recognised delivery frameworks such as Agile, Scrum, and Kanban

Job Description
As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.
Position Summary
The Automation Engineer III identifies, develops, implements, and supports automation solutions that improve manufacturing safety, quality, productivity, capacity, reliability, and cost performance. This role provides technical leadership for automation and equipment projects and serves as a key technical resource for production equipment, robotics, controls, motion systems, and equipment integration -partnering with Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Continous Improvement, Finance, Facilities, and equipment suppliers to translate production needs into reliable, scalable, financially justified solutions. The role requires broad engineering knowledge and the ability to independently manage complex assignments from opportunity identification and business-case development through design, implementation, validation, and benefits realization.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Automation & Equipment Engineering
• Identify, design, and implement automation systems -robotics, motion control, material handling, sensors, machine vision, automated inspection -that improve productivity, quality, capacity, ergonomics, and safety.
• Provide advanced engineering support and structured root-cause troubleshooting for equipment, controls, mechanical, electrical, and process issues.
• Develop corrective actions and improvements that increase equipment reliability, uptime, throughput, and maintainability.
• Monitor equipment/process performance using operational data, alarms, and downtime to identify recurring failure modes and predictive-maintenance opportunities.
• Maintain equipment configurations, specifications, control requirements, and documentation needed to keep equipment in a validated, controlled state.
Process Troubleshooting & Equipment Reliability
• Conduct manufacturing equipment failure investigations and structured troubleshooting of equipment/process failures.
• Study equipment performance and reliability trends; participate in defining preventive-maintenance schedules, procedures, and spare-parts strategies.
• Oversee adherence to maintenance and calibration schedules and ensure activities are properly documented; support complex equipment issues, including off-shift as needed.
Automation Project Leadership
• Lead automation projects end-to-end -from opportunity identification through implementation and sustained operation -working directly with stakeholders to understand process challenges and opportunities.
• Develop technical concepts, feasibility studies, scope, cost estimates, schedules, risk assessments, and business cases; evaluate opportunities by feasibility, value, and risk.
• Support CAPEX planning and technical justification; coordinate cross-functional teams and manage projects to scope, schedule, budget, and expected outcomes.
Installation, Integration & Validation
• Define facility, utility, safety, and production requirements for new automated equipment.
• Coordinate installation, commissioning, FAT/SAT testing, and production handoff; perform or support IQ/OQ/PQ and develop test plans and acceptance criteria.
• Support new product/process introduction and ensure equipment design considers reliability, maintainability, usability, and safety.
Vendor & Technology Management

• Implementation experience with leading technologies in data governance, catalogue, Data Quality, observability, MDM or cloud data platforms.

Your impact
Are you ready to make an impact and gain hands-on experience working on real-world projects from day one?

Our 13 weeks Summer Placement Programme gives you the chance to work on meaningful projects alongside subject matter experts, within multidisciplinary teams, and across the product lifecycle. Supportability Engineers are integral to a product’s lifecycle: from concept and initial design, through production, and into in-service support.
They analyse and report on the Reliability, Maintainability and Testability (RMT) of a product and advise on design and development in order to satisfy customer specifications. Supportability Engineering are the experts in Root Cause Analysis and are integral during production when manufacturing defects are observed.
As a Summer Placement Supportability Engineer, you will contribute to a real ongoing project within the department alongside experienced engineers who will provide training, mentoring and guidance. You will be exposed to real-world engineering and learn about the use of Supportability processes and tools.

• IRCM (Infra-Red Counter Measures) Systems
• Laser Target Designator and Laser Ranging Systems
• Eurofighter Typhoon Radar
• SAAB Gripen Radar
• Surveillance AESA (Active Electronically Scanned Array) Radars
• The Global Combat Air Programme

• Physics of Failure & Finite Element Analysis – an evaluation of Ansys Sherlock in addition to experience of other tools within Ansys suite
• Electronics Reliability Analysis - Evaluating Radar PCAs for Reliability, Maintainability, and Testability
• Lead Free & Materials Science – design, development and production support and interaction with engineers in a variety of functions and roles
• Data Analytics – producing reports using analysis from Production and Field Defect Data

Norton Rose Fulbright is a global law firm with more than 3,000 lawyers advising clients across locations in the United States, Europe, Canada, Latin America, Asia, Australia, Africa and the Middle East. With over 7,000 employees worldwide, our culture is the thread that connects us. Our strategy and culture are closed connected – defined by shared ambition, global collaboration and a one-team mindset. Alongside the right skills and experience, we are looking for people who are innovative, commercially minded, and motivated by the impact of the work they do – ready to share in our ambition and help shape what comes next.
Because while individuals can do well, together we achieve something extraordinary.
Role Purpose
We are building a new R&D capability focused on developing data-driven and AI-enabled products for legal services and the wider business of law.
The Data Scientist & Engineer will work within R&D alongside the Data Programme to build the foundational data capabilities required for those products: trusted, reusable data assets, reliable pipelines, data quality, lakehouse models and analytical products. These capabilities will support R&D products, AI applications, client intelligence and firm-wide decision support.
This is a hands-on hybrid data-engineering and applied-data-science role, with particular responsibility for building data products in Microsoft Fabric and Databricks. You will work with Data Programme colleagues to turn priority sources into governed, use-case-ready data assets using agreed patterns, without duplicating enterprise platform responsibilities.
You will join a small, hands-on multidisciplinary team working collaboratively across discovery, prototyping, engineering, productionisation and continuous improvement.
Key Responsibilities
•
Partner with the Data Programme, data owners and system teams to assess, access and combine priority internal and external data sources, understanding quality, permissions and fitness for use.
•
Design, build and operate reliable pipelines in Microsoft Fabric and Databricks to ingest, clean, standardise, enrich, version and publish structured, semi-structured and unstructured data as reusable data assets.
•
Create scalable lakehouse data models, schemas, data contracts and reusable features for entities such as clients, organisations, people, matters, sectors, jurisdictions, opportunities and legal topics.
•
Implement data-quality checks, lineage, provenance, observability, monitoring and change management within Fabric and Databricks workflows so data assets remain trusted over time.
•
Conduct exploratory data analysis to surface patterns, gaps, anomalies and data-quality issues, and identify opportunities for analysis, modelling or product use.
•
Develop, compare and validate appropriate statistical and machine-learning models for classification, ranking, recommendation, forecasting, anomaly detection, similarity or extraction problems.
•
Use NLP, embeddings and LLM-assisted techniques responsibly for classification, entity resolution, information extraction, clustering and relationship discovery across document-heavy data.
•
Publish curated datasets, features and analytical outputs through approved Fabric and Databricks data products, tables, APIs, search indexes, batch pipelines or product features.
•
Maintain reproducible code, tests, model and data documentation, evaluation evidence and clear statements of limitations and appropriate use.
•
Use AI agents and coding assistants responsibly to accelerate exploratory work, pipeline development, testing and documentation, while retaining ownership of analytical judgement and verification.
Initial Focus
•
Establish foundational, governed and permission-aware data assets in Microsoft Fabric and Databricks, including curated datasets, metadata, lakehouse data models and quality measures.
•
Develop reusable pipelines in Microsoft Fabric and Databricks for entity resolution, enrichment, metadata, relationship mapping and data-quality monitoring.
•
Run EDA and model development that increases the value of priority data assets for client intelligence, opportunity identification, pricing, matter analysis and other high-value use cases.
What Success Looks Like
•
The Data Programme and R&D teams can use documented, quality-controlled data assets in Fabric and Databricks without repeatedly cleaning and reconciling source data.
•
Analytical work identifies useful signals and viable opportunities, with transparent baselines, validation and limitations.
•
Successful models and features move beyond notebooks into maintainable Fabric and Databricks pipelines, APIs or products.
Essential Skills and Experience
•
At least three years' professional experience in a hybrid data-engineering and applied-data-science role, including delivery of reliable pipelines, reusable data assets and useful analytical models in Microsoft Fabric and Databricks.
•
Advanced Python, SQL and PySpark, including experience with data transformation, analysis and common machine-learning libraries.
•
Hands-on experience designing and operating scalable data pipelines, lakehouse data models, Delta and SQL transformations, and data-quality controls in Microsoft Fabric and Databricks.
•
Strong grounding in exploratory data analysis, statistics, feature engineering, model selection, validation and error analysis.
•
Practical experience with NLP, information extraction, entity resolution, embeddings or other techniques relevant to document-heavy and relationship-rich data.
•
Good understanding of data lineage, provenance, metadata, access controls, permissions and the responsible use of sensitive data within an enterprise data estate.
•
Experience with Git, automated testing, API integration, CI/CD and version-controlled deployment of data workloads in Microsoft Fabric and Databricks.
•
Ability to translate a business question into a well-formed analytical problem and communicate findings, uncertainty and trade-offs clearly.
•
Proficiency with AI agents and agentic development workflows, coupled with rigorous validation of code, data transformations and analytical conclusions.
Desirable Skills and Experience
•
Experience with Azure Data Lake, Azure Data Factory, dbt, Airflow, MLflow, Power BI, Microsoft Purview or comparable tools.
•
Experience with search indexes, vector databases, graph databases, knowledge graphs, ontologies or master-data-management…

Team: Song AI & Data – AI & Modelling Craft, UK&I
Location: London / Manchester

We Are
Accenture Song accelerates growth and value for our clients through sustained customer relevance. Our capabilities span ideation to execution: growth, product and experience design; technology and experience platforms; creative, media and marketing strategy; and campaign, content and channel orchestration. With strong client relationships and deep industry expertise, we help our clients operate efficiently and sustainably through the unlimited potential of imagination, technology and intelligence.
Visit us at: https://www.accenture.com/gb-en/about/accenture-song-index
The Team
Within Accenture Song sits AI & Data, the practice that builds the data-led intelligence behind the customer work. Song AI & Data helps organisations unlock value from data, analytics and AI by creating more relevant, personalised and effective customer experiences. Our expertise spans customer insight, data strategy and platforms, advanced analytics, performance optimisation, and AI (including generative AI and agentic AI) transformation.
You will join the Song AI & Data UK practice, within the AI & Modelling Craft: a community of data scientists, AI engineers, modellers and solution architects focused on applying AI, machine learning and advanced analytics to solve customer and growth challenges. Our teams work across the full lifecycle, from identifying opportunities and designing solutions through to building, deploying and operating AI products that deliver measurable business value.
The Role
Generative AI is moving from experimentation into enterprise delivery, and the gap between a compelling demonstration and a production-ready solution remains significant. Solutions that succeed at scale must be reliable, secure, cost-effective and capable of delivering measurable business outcomes.
As an AI Technical Delivery Manager, you will be the hands-on technical lead for the delivery of customer AI and agentic solutions. You will lead a team of AI engineers and data scientists day to day, own the technical quality of what is built, review code and designs, and make sure the solution moves from proof of concept into a production service that runs reliably.
The role combines technical leadership, engineering quality and delivery accountability for your engagement.
You will make the day-to-day technical decisions that determine whether the solution works, performs and can be supported, and you will keep the delivery lead and client stakeholders informed about progress, risks and trade-offs.
You will work across customer-facing AI use cases including personalisation, customer decisioning, customer service agents, retrieval-augmented generation solutions and agentic workflows.
This is a technical role.
You will be expected to read and review code, understand how the models, prompts, retrieval and agent orchestration actually behave, and step in to unblock the team when needed. You will be leading engineers rather than doing all the engineering yourself, but you need to know the work well enough to set the standard, spot problems early and hold your own with experienced engineers and architects.
What You Will Do
• Lead the technical delivery of customer AI and agentic solutions, owning the day-to-day technical plan, task breakdown, sequencing and technical quality across the engineering team.
• Review code, prompts, retrieval pipelines, agent designs and evaluation results, giving clear feedback and making sure what is merged meets the agreed standards.
• Lead technical design within the engagement, covering model selection, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic workflows, evaluation frameworks, guardrails, scalability and cost, working with the solution architect where one is assigned.
• Identify technical and delivery risks early, including data quality issues, integration complexity, performance bottlenecks, cost overruns and operational readiness concerns, and raise them with the delivery lead together with options for addressing them.
• Set up and run the engineering practices the team works to, including code review, testing, evaluation, CI/CD, environment management, monitoring and release processes.
• Assess whether proofs of concept are ready to scale, clearly explaining what has been proven, what has not and what is required before production deployment.
• Work with client technical teams on integration, environments, data access, security and deployment, and explain technical progress, issues and trade-offs to client stakeholders in plain terms.
• Lead and develop a team of AI engineers and data scientists, allocating work, coaching individuals, running technical stand-ups and design reviews, and helping people grow.
• Contribute reusable code, patterns and delivery accelerators back to the AI & Modelling Craft, and share lessons learned from live delivery.
• Support solution shaping and estimation for new work, providing technical input on approach, effort, team composition and risks.
What We Are Looking For
Core Requirements
• Hands-on AI and agentic engineering. Experience building and shipping generative AI and agentic solutions into production, including retrieval-augmented generation, LLM-powered applications and agentic workflows. You have written the code yourself on at least some of these, and you understand how prompting, context management, retrieval, tool use, orchestration, evaluation and guardrails work in practice.
• AI and data science foundations. Good understanding of machine learning and data science alongside generative AI. You know how models are trained, evaluated and monitored, and you can tell when a problem calls for predictive modelling, optimisation, generative AI, agentic AI or a combination of approaches.
• Customer AI experience. Experience applying AI to customer growth, personalisation, marketing, commerce, sales or service challenges, and an understanding of how technical decisions affect customer and business outcomes.
• Engineering and platform skills. Strong Python and software engineering skills, with working knowledge of APIs, system integration, cloud platforms (Azure, AWS or GCP), containers, CI/CD, testing and production monitoring. You can review code properly, spot design and quality problems, and give feedback engineers can act on.
• Technical leadership of engineering teams. Experience leading a team of engineers or data scientists on a delivery, setting technical direction, running reviews, resolving technical issues and being accountable for the quality and timeliness of what the team produces.
• Delivery planning and estimation. Experience breaking technical work into a plan, estimating effort, tracking progress against it and adjusting when things change. You can distinguish what a proof of concept demonstrates from what is required for production.
• Stakeholder communication.…

Role Title: Senior Power Systems Technician
Team: Power Systems Team | UK LTSA Operations
Reports to: High Voltage Technical Manager (Regional)
Region: South / North / Central (UK)
Role type: Field-based, senior technical role
Purpose
Acts as the regional senior technical specialist for power systems and product commissioning across the UK BESS fleet. Leads product commissioning of e-STORAGE products (SolBank, string inverters, MVSkids etc) to OEM standard, leads HV/MV maintenance and safety activities across e-STORAGE and third-party fleets (i.e. SMA, Power Electronics) and develops the competency of the wider service team to support HV/MV works.
Scope Definition: Product Commissioning
This role leads product commissioning of e-STORAGE products: commissioning of e-STORAGE power conversion and MV equipment to OEM standard, including first power-on initialization parameters, product-level testing, and return-to-service. The site Commissioning (Cx) team retains overall site and project commissioning ownership, including the energisation programme, grid compliance and G99 testing, punch lists, and client handover. The Power Systems Technician works within the site Cx team's sequence: the Cx team owns the programme and the date; Power Systems owns the product Cx, safety documents, and product-level sign-off within it.
MV/HV Authorisation & Control of Work
Control of work and HV authorisation are determined by contract and project phase:
• During commissioning, the EPC (or Principal Contractor) is responsible for site control of work and HV authorisation. This role operates within the EPC's safe system of work and provides product-level expertise.
• During LTSA operations, the HV authorisation and control-of-work model is defined in each contract and varies by site (client-appointed, third-party, or CSE-held). This role provides the trained, competent personnel for appointment where CSE holds or is delegated that responsibility.
• Where a third party holds HV authorisation for a site, this role coordinates, supervises interfaces, and delivers the product-level technical work within their control regime.
Key Responsibilities
Product Commissioning (e-STORAGE products)
• Lead product commissioning of e-STORAGE products across UK LTSA sites (SolBank, string inverters, MVSkids and associated MV plant) to OEM standard and project scope.
• Own and set first power-on initialization parameters (OEM-trained personnel requirement per product manuals); incorrect settings risk equipment damage and certification non-compliance.
• Own product commissioning standards, procedures, test records, and documentation packs; ensure consistency across all UK projects.
• Provide product-level technical support to the site Cx team during energisation.
• Support the site Cx team during SAT and witness testing; provide product-level technical sign-off.
HV/MV Operations & Safety
• Competent for appointment to carry out MV/HV isolations, earthing, and safety document duties under the prevailing site safe system of work, as a mandatory precursor to intrusive PM/CM works. Site HV authorisation arrangements are defined per contract and phase (see MV/HV Authorisation & Control of Work).
• Carry out operational HV/MV switching during the service phase, including switching for planned PM outages, CM interventions, and restoration on return to service, where CSE holds control of work under the contract.
• Provide HV/MV support to the service team during PM and CM activities: isolations, earthing, switching, and safe access where service team work interfaces with HV/MV plant.
• Lead HV/MV preventative maintenance across CSE, SMA and Power Electronics MV skids, RMUs, transformers, and protection systems per OEM schedules.
• Lead corrective maintenance and fault investigation on HV/MV equipment: root cause analysis, rectification and return to service.
• Provide safety leadership and oversight for all HV/MV activities in region, including supervision of third-party HV contractors where used.
Technical Expertise & Capability Building
• Subject-matter expert across all inverter platforms (CSE string inverters, SMA, Power Electronics) for HV/MV maintenance activities; product commissioning expertise applies to e-STORAGE products.
• Assess and develop service team competency for HV/MV support roles; deliver toolbox talks, training, and authorisation recommendations.
• Feed field learnings back into standards, RAMS/SOPs, and OEM escalations.
Out of Scope
• Routine non-HV/MV maintenance (LV PM, BESS enclosure servicing, HVAC, general CM). This is delivered by the regional service team, with this role providing HV oversight only where work interfaces with HV/MV plant.
Requirements
• Trained and competent for MV/HV activities to 33kV; capable of appointment under company or client operational rules as contracts require.
• Time-served electrical background with utility-scale BESS or solar commissioning experience.
• Working knowledge of MV switchgear, transformers, and protection systems.
• Familiarity with G99 requirements sufficient to support the site Cx team during compliance testing.
• Full UK driving licence; regional and occasional national travel.

You'll work at the intersection of customers, business, data and innovation, helping us respond to some of society's biggest challenges including an ageing population, changing retirement expectations, low confidence in managing money and the transfer of wealth between generations.

You'll thrive if you're curious and open-minded, comfortable challenging the status quo, interested in customers and what drives their decisions, analytical and commercially aware, collaborative and relationship-focused, and motivated to make a positive impact.

What you'll learn
You'll build a broad understanding of our customers, products, propositions and commercial strategy while developing skills that will support your long-term career.
The impact you'll make
During your rotations, you could use customer insight and data to identify opportunities for improvement, support projects that influence future products and propositions, help improve customer experiences and journeys, contribute to strategic decisions that shape our business, work across teams and generate insights that support senior decision-making.
Most importantly, you'll help us deliver better outcomes for customers while gaining exposure to the challenges and opportunities shaping the future of financial services.
We'll invest in you
Alongside hands-on experience, you'll benefit from a structured learning and development journey designed to accelerate your growth.
We'll help you build the confidence, commercial understanding and leadership skills needed to succeed in Wealth and Insurance.
Why Wealth and Insurance?
The world is changing. Customers' expectations are evolving, technology is transforming our industry and financial confidence has never been more important.
That's why we're investing in the next generation of talent. People who can combine commercial thinking, customer understanding, digital capability and fresh perspectives to help shape our future.
Requirements
What you need to apply
•
Be in your penultimate year at university.
•
Be a problem solver who brings a STEM mindset, using data and logic while staying curious about people and how organisations work
•

Edinburgh and Leeds. We support hybrid working, where you’ll be expected to spend a minimum of two days each week in the office where you have been placed.

Applications for our Wealth and Insurance Industrial Placement open on 10th September and close on 8th November.

About the Hiring Team
Level Infinite is Tencent’s global gaming brand. It is a global game publisher offering a comprehensive network of services for games, development teams, and studios around the world.
We are dedicated to delivering engaging and original gaming experiences to a worldwide audience, whenever and wherever they choose to play while building a community that fosters inclusivity, connection, and accessibility. Level Infinite also provides a wide range of services and resources to our network of developers and partner studios around the world to help them unlock the true potential of their games.
What the Role Entails
We are hiring a research intern to train LLM agents that play in-game characters. The agent has to stay in persona across multi-turn dialogue, use memory and game context, and keep relationship, tone, and world rules intact. The work sits on a live role-play NPC model: supervised fine-tuning today, with preference optimization and verifiable-reward reinforcement learning as the next training stages.
1. Train role-play agents with supervised fine-tuning (SFT), then post-train them with direct preference optimization (DPO) and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Iterate on persona consistency, multi-turn coherence, and instruction following.
2. Build and curate SFT, preference, and verifiable-reward data for character dialogue, covering memory injection, relationship stage, language switching, emotion, and out-of-character resistance.
3. Design checks that can be verified automatically, such as format, language, persona boundaries, and safety refusals, and use them both as RLVR rewards and as offline regression tests.
4. Work with game designers and engineers to bring the agent into a live game, and keep latency, cost, and player experience within production constraints.
Who We Look For
1. Currently enrolled in a Master's or PhD program in Computer Science, NLP, Machine Learning, or a related field, or recently graduated. Available at least three days per week, with supervisor and university approval where required.
2. Fluent English (written and spoken) and strong communication skills are required. You will work closely with game designers, engineers, and researchers across regions, and must be able to explain experiment results and trade-offs clearly.
3. Hands-on experience with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of LLMs, and with post-training methods including DPO and RLVR (or a closely related verifiable-reward RL method). You should be able to run the loop from data and training config through evaluation and the next iteration.
4. Experience training or evaluating role-play or character-dialogue models, including persona consistency, multi-turn dialogue, and staying in character.
5. Proficient in Python and PyTorch, and comfortable with the Hugging Face / Transformers training stack.
6. Preferred: experience with LLM agents (memory, planning, or tool use), LLM applications in games, or a publication at a major NLP/ML venue (ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML).

Our Business and Legal Operations Graduate Scheme is a two-year programme encompassing every aspect of the rapid changes currently underway in the delivery of high-end legal services. This doesn't just involve the emergence of new technology. It involves the increasingly crucial role played by other technical disciplines in providing more complex and sophisticated client solutions and optimising our performance as a business.

The Business and Legal Operations Graduate Scheme develops people who can help turn those expectations into action.
What can you expect?
Graduates will have the opportunity to complete four six-month rotations across various teams and programme areas. Throughout the programme, graduates will gain experience across a broad range of work supporting both clients and the firm.

• Helping teams improve how legal matters are planned and delivered through project management, process improvement, technology adoption, reporting and legal service design;
• Working with lawyers, consultants and technology specialists to understand client needs and help develop practical services, products and solutions;
• Supporting the business operations of legal teams through a client secondment opportunity, gaining first-hand insight into client priorities and ways of working; and
• Supporting projects that help shape the future of Norton Rose Fulbright, from AI adoption and business transformation programmes to process improvement and change initiatives.
No two rotations will be the same. Graduates could be:
• Uncovering a business or client challenge and identifying opportunities for improvement;
• Designing and testing a new legal product or tool;
• Delivering training sessions on new technology;
• Running workshops with clients' in-house legal teams;
• Turning raw data into insights that shape decision-making;
• Coordinating projects from scoping through to completion;
• Creating proposals, presentations and training materials; or
• Working alongside lawyers, technologists and consultants.

Ever thought about working on the largest space craft in the UK? Because that's what we do in Portsmouth; we design, build and test satellites!

There are few other experiences like that!

• We’re part of Airbus Defence and Space – the biggest space company in Europe, and a major player in the UK’s growing space sector;

Over 95% of all apprentices who successfully complete the programme move into permanent roles within the business. Many of our senior leaders and early career managers were apprentices.
Many apprentices go onto further education, supported by the business.
Airbus is a multinational business, supported by businesses, suppliers and customers around the world. Many roles will require travel.

We want to get to know you—not just your grades or school background so, tell us on your cover letter:

What is it about Airbus that makes you excited to start a career with us? What is it about our company, our values, or the future of the space sector that excites you? We want to hear about what motivates you to pursue this unique path and how you see yourself growing with us.

Department: Bioanalytical Laboratory
Location: Onsite; York, UK

SUMMARY
A Technical Specialist is responsible for the development, validation, troubleshooting, and lifecycle management of ligand binding assays (LBAs) supporting regulated (GLP/GCP) and non-regulated bioanalytical studies. RESPONSIBILITIES
• Scientific, Technical and Regulatory: Act as the technical subject-matter expert (SME) for large molecule bioanalysis (PK/TK, ADA, biomarkers), Design, develop, validate, and implement robust LBA methods in line with current regulatory guidance, Independently manage method development, transfer, validation, and study support activities, Provide scientific and technical leadership, ensuring appropriate assay design and data integrity, Lead troubleshooting of assays and instrumentation, providing timely support to laboratory teams, Ensure all bioanalytical work is conducted in full compliance with GLP/GCP requirements, Maintain oversight of analytical platforms (e.g. ELISA, MSD) and supporting laboratory equipment, Lead equipment lifecycle management, including evaluation, procurement, qualification, and validation, Support and oversee computerised system validation (CSV) and software compliance activities, Ensure compliance with COSHH, health & safety, and environmental regulations, Lead or support laboratory investigations, deviations, and CAPA management, Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance assay robustness, efficiency, and data quality, Oversee the review and approval of SOPs, ensuring alignment with regulatory expectations, Support internal and external audits/inspections, including resolution of findings, Provide hands-on technical guidance and mentorship to laboratory scientists, Act as a point of escalation for complex scientific or operational challenges, Promote a culture of quality, compliance, and scientific excellence within the laboratory, Maintain current knowledge of GLP, GCP, and industry best practices in bioanalysis, Ensure all activities are conducted in a safe, compliant, and inspection-ready manner, Demonstrate ownership, accountability, and proactive problem-solving across all responsibilities.
• People: Act as a mentor and technical trainer for Laboratory Scientists; support recruitment and onboarding activities as required, Partner with departmental management to ensure effective team and individual performance, aligned to business objectives, Provide clear, actionable feedback to support prioritisation and delivery against critical timelines and commitments, Support optimisation of laboratory resourcing (people, equipment, facilities) to ensure efficient and effective study delivery, Drive the ACM Mission, Vision and Core Values with every interaction, Foster a culture of quality, compliance, safety, customer focus, and individual accountability.
• Strategic and Financial: Support Operational Management in the development and execution of long-term business and operational strategies, Monitor and interpret financial and operational metrics, using data to inform decision-making, resource allocation, and process improvements, Provide timely, transparent updates to management on laboratory performance, risks, and any deviations from agreed objectives, Drive and track key performance indicators (KPIs) to ensure high levels of productivity, efficiency, and customer satisfaction.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

As a Senior ROV Pilot Technician, you’ll support the Supervisor in ensuring the smooth operation and maintenance of Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) systems and all associated tooling. You’ll work across a varied range of offshore projects throughout the UK, the North Sea, wider Europe, and parts of Africa, covering workscopes such as renewables, oil and gas, survey operations, light construction, and drill‑support activities.

Maintain a strong safety focus with a proactive attitude toward Health, Safety, and the Environment, adhering to Fugro’s safety standards and core values.

Lead maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair activities for ROV systems, including associated subsea equipment and tooling.

Support the Supervisor with operational planning, safety documentation, and technical coordination across offshore projects.

Proven expertise in at least one core technical discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, hydraulic), with working knowledge across other related fields.

Competent in piloting ROVs and operating manipulators with precision and control during offshore operations.
•
Hands‑on experience with various ROV systems, subsea tooling, and Launch and Recovery Systems (LARS).
•
Background in diverse subsea operations and adaptability to different offshore environments and conditions.
•
Experience supporting mobilisations and demobilisations as part of a collaborative offshore team.

Strong safety awareness, consistently working to the highest standards in line with the company’s Safety Management System.

Effective communicator, especially in emergency situations, with the ability to coordinate well with team members.

Willingness to work on both vessels and platforms.

Do you want to join our Geo-data revolution? Fugro’s global reach and unique know-how will put the world at your fingertips. For individuals who can take the initiative, but work well within a team.

At Fugro, our people are our superpower. Their variety of viewpoints, experiences, knowledge and talents give us collective strength. Principal FPGA Design Engineer

We have opportunities for ambitious FPGA Engineers at Principal level to join our multidisciplinary engineering team at the forefront of additive manufacturing technology.

Working within Research & Development, you will contribute to the full product lifecycle, from concept and architecture through verification, release to production, and long-term support.
These are hands-on engineering roles, combining FPGA design, verification and hardware bring-up with close collaboration across electronics, software, systems, algorithms and mechanical engineering teams. Depending on experience and grade, you will also provide technical leadership, influence engineering strategy, and mentor developing engineers.
The FPGA frequently interfaces with high-speed digital electronics, embedded processors, sensors and analogue circuitry. As such, a strong appreciation of system-level design and hardware/software interaction is essential.

FPGA Design & Development
•
Develop FPGA architectures and RTL designs from concept through to production release.
•
Design, implement and maintain high-quality VHDL solutions with a focus on performance, reliability, portability and efficient resource utilisation.
•
Perform timing analysis, constraint development, timing closure and design optimisation.
•
Implement and verify FPGA functionality in both simulation and on target hardware.
•
Develop reusable and maintainable IP blocks and design frameworks for use across multiple projects and product generations.
•
Support product sustainment, issue investigation and design improvements throughout the product lifecycle.
Verification & Validation

Develop robust verification environments using modern methodologies including OSVVM and VUnit.
•
Create reusable, self-checking testbenches with measurable verification coverage.

Define verification strategies, plans and acceptance criteria.

Drive continuous improvement in simulation, regression testing and automated verification workflows.

Support hardware validation, debugging and system integration activities.
Systems & Product Development
•
Capture, analyse and refine requirements, ensuring clear traceability from customer and system requirements through to implementation and verification.
•
Work closely with systems, electronics, software, algorithms and test engineers to deliver integrated solutions.

Evaluate and implement signal processing, control and embedded algorithms within FPGA architectures.
•
Contribute to safety, reliability and compliance activities, including design assurance and audit-ready engineering evidence.
•
Produce and maintain high-quality technical documentation, including architecture specifications, interface definitions, verification reports and design rationale.
Strategic & Architectural Leadership
•
Define FPGA architecture roadmaps and technical direction across multiple products and programmes.
•
Assess and introduce new technologies, design methodologies and verification approaches.
•
Act as a recognised subject matter expert for FPGA and digital systems engineering.

Influence system-level architecture decisions and long-term technology strategy.

Degree in Electronic Engineering, Physics, Computer Engineering or a related discipline.
•
Strong commercial experience developing FPGA solutions using VHDL.

Solid understanding of digital design principles, including: Timing analysis and timing closureClock domain crossing techniquesReset architecturesPipelining and resource optimisationHigh-speed digital interfaces

Experience implementing and verifying FPGA designs in simulation and on hardware.
•
Understanding of FPGA development tools and design flows.
•
Ability to communicate effectively within a multidisciplinary engineering team.
•
Extensive experience leading the architecture and development of complex FPGA-centric products.
•
Recognised expertise in FPGA design, verification and system integration.
•
Track record of influencing engineering strategy and technology direction.
•
Strong capability in technical leadership across multiple programmes and engineering disciplines.
•
Experience defining engineering processes, standards and verification methodologies.

•
Experience with Intel (Altera) FPGA devices and Quartus development tools.
•
Experience of OSVVM, VUnit and modern verification methodologies.
•
Familiarity with VS Code, Active-HDL or equivalent simulation environments.
•
Knowledge of embedded software development using C, C++ or Python.
•
Experience with Git, Azure DevOps and continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) workflows.
•
Understanding of DSP, control systems and numerical algorithms.
•
Knowledge of high-speed digital design, EMC and mixed-signal electronics.
•
Experience working within regulated or safety-conscious product development environments.
Person Specification
You are a passionate and capable engineer who enjoys solving complex technical challenges and delivering robust, high-quality products.
You combine strong FPGA design expertise with a systems-level mindset and are comfortable working across disciplinary boundaries. You communicate clearly, collaborate effectively and take ownership of technical outcomes.
At Principal level, you are a recognised technical authority who influences product architecture, engineering strategy and organisational capability while continuing to engage with hands-on engineering challenges.

flir.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/flircareers/j.description_excerpt:
Be visionary
Teledyne Technologies Incorporated provides enabling technologies for industrial growth markets that require advanced technology and high reliability. These markets include aerospace and defense, factory automation, air and water quality environmental monitoring, electronics design and development, oceanographic research, deepwater oil and gas exploration and production, medical imaging and pharmaceutical research.​
We are looking for individuals who thrive on making an impact and want the excitement of being on a team that wins.
Job Description
Senior Software Engineer - Flight Data Analysis Software
Uxbridge, West London, 4 days onsite, 1 day from home
Every commercial flight records thousands of parameters — control inputs, engine performance, altitude, warnings. When the aircraft lands, that data has to be retrieved, decoded and turned into something an airline's safety team can act on. We build the software that does it. Over 300 airlines use our ground systems, including most of the world's major carriers, alongside military operators. When an airline spots an unstable approach trend before it becomes an incident, our software is usually how they found it.
We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join the team in Uxbridge that builds it.
What you'll actually do
You'll own features end to end — from design discussion through to release — across a stack that spans a mature .NET backend, Angular front ends, and Python tooling. Specifically:
• Design and build backend services and APIs that process large volumes of flight data, where performance and correctness genuinely matter
• Take technical ownership of a product area: make the architectural calls, and be the person the team asks about it
• Review other engineers' code and mentor two or three developers earlier in their careers
• Work with QA, product and the engineering lead across a normal Agile cycle — planning, standups, reviews, retros
• Help us modernise: we have a long-lived .NET codebase with some older Windows service components, and part of this role is bringing it forward sensibly rather than rewriting for its own sake
What we need
• Around 4+ years building production software commercially
• Strong C#/.NET and solid relational database skills (we use MySQL)
• Comfortable working across the stack — you don't have to be a front-end specialist, but you should be able to work in TypeScript/Angular when a feature needs it
• Experience designing and consuming RESTful APIs
• Genuinely good at debugging: the ability to work out why a system is misbehaving from incomplete information
• Git and modern version control workflows
Useful, but we'll teach you
• Python
• AWS (EC2, Lambda, S3, RDS)
• Docker and CI/CD pipelines
• Automated testing frameworks
• Aviation or aerospace domain knowledge — almost nobody arrives with this, and we don't expect you to
You do not need to tick every box. If you're strong on the backend and curious about the rest, apply.
What we offer
As part of the wider Teledyne UK group, we offer our employees a range of company benefits that include:
•
• Salary sacrifice-led pension plan that matches employee contributions up to 7%.
• Employee Stock Purchase Plan.
• Free life assurance cover at the value of four times basic annual salary.
• ⁠Salary sacrifice Electric & Hybrid Vehicle car scheme
• 25 days holiday per annum, plus bank holidays.
• Holiday purchase scheme which enables employees to purchase an additional 5 days worth of annual leave each year.
• Company funded medical cash plan (MediCash) which allows eligible members to offset the cost of routine medical treatments.
• Internal reward and recognition scheme linked to internal benefits platform.
• Employee Assistance Programme.
• Comprehensive wellbeing programme that supports employees with their physical, mental and financial health, as well as their cultural/environmental wellbeing.
• Competitive employee discounts platform that provides employees with discounts with leading brands/retailers.
• Cycle to Work scheme.
• Enhanced family-friendly benefits and policies.
• Company sick pay.
• Free Onsite parking
• Career development across the wider Teledyne group — a lot of our engineers have moved between teams, sites and disciplines
• Software that matters: what you ship affects how safely aircraft are operated
The commute, honestly
We're onsite four days a week with one day from home. We know that rules us out for some people. But if you live anywhere in West London, Hillingdon, Buckinghamshire or along the M4/M40, this is likely the shortest commute you'll find for a role at this level — Uxbridge is the end of the Metropolitan and Piccadilly lines, and there's parking. Several of our team took this job specifically to stop commuting into central London.
Interview process
• A Teams call with the hiring manager and site manager — informal, both ways
• An onsite session covering technical discussion and a paired programming task, plus competency-based questions with our Head of Digital Solutions
• Offer
About Teledyne Controls
Since 1964 we've designed and manufactured aircraft data recording and management systems, working directly with airlines and with OEMs including Airbus and Boeing. Teledyne Controls Flight Data Company in Uxbridge is our principal UK office, where we develop the ground-based software used to replay and analyse recorded flight data.
Teledyne and all of our employees are committed to conducting business with the highest ethical standards. We require all employees to comply with all applicable laws, regulations, rules and regulatory orders. Our reputation for honesty, integrity and high ethics is as important to us as our reputation for making innovative sensing solutions.

Job Description:
Our M&A Tax team is structured in a unique way – we are focused on providing the full spectrum of tax services to private equity, across funds, deals and portfolio companies on a wide scope of transactional work both domestically and internationally.
We are leading advisers to mid-market private equity firms and large acquisitive corporates with deal values of anywhere from a few million to over a billion. We support our clients throughout the entire deal lifecycle from the initial proposal stage and assisting with offer terms, undertaking due diligence and advice on the acquisition structure through to completion and post-deal advice.
We work with businesses across a huge range of sectors – from technology and gaming, through to care homes, art galleries, travel and retail. This is a fast-moving and exciting environment. It is technically led but with a keen eye on service and so this role will involve technical tax application, extensive interaction with clients and great interpersonal and organisational skills.
M&A Tax are a small, tight-knit team, and have experienced exceptional growth year on year. We have a strong pipeline and as part of a growing team, you will have significant opportunities to take on responsibility and develop as the team grows.
We are looking for bright and enthusiastic individuals who are looking to step up into a Manager role and are interested in a career in M&A tax.

A look into the role
As a Manager in M&A Tax team, you will provide tax structuring advice and will undertake tax due diligence on both buy-side and sell-side transactions for private equity and corporate clients. You may also have the opportunity to work on public company transactions, primarily on AIM and the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange.
If you enjoy working on a variety of projects and sectors, you’ll fit right in. Here are some things you can expect from a role in M&A Tax:

• You will be responsible for leading due diligence meetings with the target business, overseeing the due diligence analysis and reviewing reports to ensure they have been accurately and robustly prepared ahead of final review by the partner/director.

• You will manage project budgets, ensuring bills are raised accurately and promptly, fees are collected in a timely manner and debtors kept to a minimum.

• UK corporation tax compliance and/or M&A experience
• Exposure to other tax issues – transfer pricing, R&D, VAT, employment taxes, stamp duty, share transactions/share option schemes
• Proven experience in client handling and project management, building and sustaining relationships
• Experience of advising on technical tax matters is essential
• Demonstrable experience of managing multiple deliverables, showing prioritisation skills and meeting deadlines within an expected timeframe
• Strong Excel and Power Point skills to prepare client and target documentation.
Knowing we’re right for you
The culture at Grant Thornton is what sets us apart, we’re known for our inclusive culture and creating environments where all our people can flourish. The things that set you apart, we value them, and this helps us all to perform at our best.
Our values are the unwavering principles that shape our daily behaviours and decisions, alongside our drive to do the right thing. We’re looking for people who align with our values and are purposefully driven, actively curious and candid but kind. You can learn more about our values in practice here.

Benefits including pension, life assurance and private medical, additional holiday purchasing and health benefits

Amex GBT is a place where colleagues find inspiration in travel as a force for good and – through their work – can make an impact on our industry. We’re here to help our colleagues achieve success and offer an inclusive and collaborative culture where your voice is valued.

• You’ll be a lead for Amex GBT’s mid-market EMEA sales development team. Your mandate is to build, coach, and drive a high-performance team that creates qualified pipeline through a phone-first, conversation-driven outbound approach.
• Hands-On Coaching & Real-Time Development: This is where you live. You’re listening to calls, with reps during prospecting blocks, running live coaching sessions, and showing your team what a great outbound conversation actually sounds like. You don’t wait for a weekly 1:1 to develop someone—you do it in the moment, every day.

You understand which initiatives are driving results, where friction exists, and what your team needs next. What we're looking for
• You’re a leader your team respects deeply—not because of your title, but because they’ve seen you in the work alongside them. You combine a genuine love for coaching and developing people with the strategic sharpness to drive consistent results.
• A proven coaching-first leadership approach—you believe your primary job is to develop every person on your team, and your track record reflects it
• Deep belief in a phone-first outbound model. You understand that real pipeline is built through conversations, not just sequences and automation
• Strong creative instincts for outbound strategy—you bring ideas on messaging, positioning, and account engagement that go beyond the standard playbook
• Naturally curious about the business, the market, and your team’s prospects. You ask why before you prescribe how
• Comfortable and confident picking up the phone yourself. You lead by example and never ask your team to do something you wouldn’t do
• Data-literate and capable of building your own reports when needed, but you use data to drive coaching and decisions—not to avoid being present

• Strong cross-functional collaborator who represents the sales development organization with credibility and professionalism
