Job Description
Are you passionate about making a difference and helping others?
Would you like to work in a role that puts the customer at the heart of everything we do, making a genuine positive impact?
Then consider the role of a Progression Coach at Reed in Partnership!
This role is office based, but will involve travel across Kent & Sussex also.
Please Note, these roles are expressions of interest only at this point. We are currently working on a number of exciting opportunities within this area and are looking to build a pipeline of talent to allow us to work quickly upon contract award. We will be in a position to be able to begin the formal recruitment process in the coming weeks and we will be in touch to discuss the next steps of your expression of interest as soon as possible.
Who we are:
Reed's Employability Division aims to positively transform lives by helping individuals who are unemployed, economically inactive, or facing challenges such as health conditions, disabilities, or caring responsibilities to find sustainable employment. Through a wide range of tailored support services including one-to-one careers guidance, CV writing, interview preparation, and skills training, we have supported over 250,000 people on their journey into work.
The new Confident Futures programme, funded by the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), is designed to support Universal Credit claimants with long-term health conditions. It is a voluntary programme focused on helping participants move closer to work by improving confident, wellbeing, skills, stability and readiness for work.
What is the role about?
A Progression Coach is responsible for the attraction, registration and progression of Participants to achieve placements. A Progression Coach will use a variety of techniques including effective diagnosis, individual coaching and training, action planning and Health & Wellbeing Support to provide intensive personal support to a caseload of up to 25 Participants. Progression Coaches will deliver our services both in fixed Reed in Partnership locations, co-location sites and where appropriate within community venues, to ensure our services are accessible to all.
Just some of your day-to-day responsibilities will include:
Attraction & Enlisting
•
Pitches and sells Reed in Partnership as the partner of choice in Welfare to Work.
•
Develops own knowledge of Reed in Partnership and the relevant programme in order to enlist Participants.
•
Builds and maintains relationships with the Job Centre Plus and other relevant Partners through regular telephone contact, visits and newsletters as appropriate to ensure Participants are aware of our services and to allay any concerns they may have with accessing or utilising our services.
Engagement and Diagnosis
•
Provides a good customer service to Participants including meeting and greeting Participants in a professional way.
•
Explains our service offering (details of the programme) including ensuring the Participant understands their rights and responsibilities (e.g. complaints & feedback process), whilst registering the Participant in accordance to contractual obligations and eligibility criteria.
•
Ensure Initial Assessments focus on getting to know the participant, understanding their motivation for joining the programme (if voluntary participation) and exploration of their aspirations and needs.
•
Identifies and utilises various approaches where appropriate such as visionary goal setting, and applicable financial incentives to sell the benefits of the programme and to adequately diagnose first level barriers.
Participant Progression
•
Develops and manages Participants job goals using creative techniques and deep level questioning as necessary for the Participants needs, to assist with diagnosis and progression.
•
Motivates, encourages and empowers Participants, identifying barriers, realistic job goals and social training needs, referring as appropriate to relevant support functions
•
Collaborate with local and specialist partners to provide wraparound/holistic support that addresses multiple/complex barriers (e.g. finance, housing, caring responsibilities).
•
Engage with local employers to source suitable work experience/volunteering opportunities and support inclusive recruitment/job-carving.
Training Delivery
•
Engage and empower Learners whilst delivering training sessions, with the aim of progressing them to achieve sustainable employment.
•
Awareness of and ability to adapt to a diverse range of learners and their learning needs and styles.
•
Follow lesson plans and activity guidance provided.

Job Description:
Department
Information Technology – Data Platform
Position Purpose
Own EDF Trading's enterprise data strategy and the capabilities required to provide trusted, governed and readily usable data. The role leads data product management, market data systems, core data engineering, plus data governance and quality. You will be accountable for turning data into a managed enterprise asset while enabling analytics, advanced modelling and AI at scale.
Main Responsibilities
• Define and execute the enterprise data strategy, target architecture, operating model and multi-year roadmap in alignment with business and technology strategy.
• Lead data product management, market data systems, core data engineering, and data governance and quality as an integrated enterprise capability.
• Establish accountable ownership for critical data domains, datasets and data products, with clear quality requirements, service expectations and lifecycle plans.
• Prioritise investment and delivery across ingestion, streaming, APIs, warehousing, reporting and advanced analytics capabilities.
• Ensure metadata, lineage, data quality controls, access controls, retention, privacy and control evidence are embedded into platforms and delivery practices.
• Build strong partnerships across the trading, operations, risk, finance and corporate functions to convert business needs into reusable data products rather than one-off pipelines.
• Own the market data capability, including distribution, entitlements, vendor strategy, usage transparency, cost management and resilience.
• Provide governed enablement for data science and AI, including trusted training data, reproducibility, model lifecycle dependencies and responsible-use controls.
• Set measures for data reliability, quality, adoption, delivery flow, platform performance, cost and value realisation.
• Develop senior leaders and specialist teams, balancing central standards with federated domain accountability and avoiding duplicated data engineering.
Experience Required
• Substantial leadership experience across enterprise data, data engineering, data governance, analytics or data product management in a complex organisation.
• Demonstrable delivery of enterprise-scale data platforms and operating models, ideally in energy trading, commodities or financial services.
• Experience managing critical market, trade, reference, risk, finance or regulatory data with demanding quality, timeliness and control requirements.
• Track record of building multidisciplinary teams and leading material change across technology and business functions.
• Experience of vendor and commercial management for data platforms, cloud services and market data providers.
• Strong executive-level communication, investment governance and benefits management experience.
Technical Requirements
• Deep understanding of modern data architecture, including event streaming, Kafka, APIs, batch ingestion, lakehouse patterns, data warehousing and real-time distribution.
• Strong knowledge of data engineering practices using SQL and relevant programming languages, storage design, performance optimisation, testing, deployment and observability.
• Practical expertise in metadata management, lineage, data quality, master and reference data, ownership models, access governance and control assurance
• Understanding of analytics, reporting, machine learning and AI lifecycles, including data preparation, feature provenance, monitoring and governance.
• Knowledge of cloud and hybrid architecture, cybersecurity, privacy, resilience, cost management and enterprise integration.
Person Specification
• Enterprise thinker who treats data as a product and a controlled asset, not simply a technology platform.
• Able to challenge local optimisation and drive reuse, standardisation and clear ownership across organisational boundaries.
• Commercially aware, evidence-led and comfortable making investment and prioritisation decisions.
• Strong communicator who can translate between executives, data specialists, engineers and control functions.
• Collaborative across business domains and able to create shared ownership of data outcomes.
• Inclusive leader who develops talent and builds a culture of quality and accountability.
Hours of Work:
8.30am – 5.30pm / 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday

11.    Lead on up-skilling Officers and Members to deliver positive change through the spatial planning process.
12.    Ensure that the necessary guidance and other resources are available to developers and planning applicants to secure healthy and inclusive design.
13.    The post holder may be called upon to provide expert advice at Planning Committee, public inquiries and hearings.
14.    Actively engaging with the broader Active Hull system and its governance structures, whilst contributing to the wider Hull place-based partnership agenda, supporting collaborative efforts across sectors.

• Good written and verbal communication skills, along with basic IT confidence.
• Strong attention to detail and the ability to keep track of tasks and share updates with the team.
• A caring, patient and non‑judgmental approach when working with people with lived experience of mental health challenges.
• Reliability and good time‑keeping.
• The ability to work collaboratively with staff and residents, while also being comfortable taking initiative or following guidance.
• An understanding of Waythrough’s work and a genuine interest in contributing to our mission and values.

Subsurface Group
Job Description:
We are hiring a Carbonate Reservoir Geologist position within our Sedimentology & Stratigraphy (SedStrat) Specialist Team. The team provides deep technical expertise that is applied globally across bp’s Exploration and Reservoir Development portfolio.
This is an individual contributor role that requires a deep understanding of carbonate depositional systems and reservoir architecture, and broad experience of carbonate reservoir production characteristics. The successful candidate must have specifically carbonate sedimentology and reservoir quality expertise with a history of successfully applying and integrating that knowledge in a variety of subsurface projects to create value. In addition, the successful candidate will be able to demonstrate strong project management abilities, as well as excellent communication and influencing skills. This role is suitable for experienced carbonate sedimentologists with a history of business delivery.
KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:
Primary accountability would be as one of bp’s recognized carbonate reservoir subject matter experts .
In addition to supporting carbonate-focused projects, the successful candidate must lead subsurface teams across bp to deliver sedimentological and reservoir characterization studies in a range of diverse carbonate settings globally.
• Integrate diverse subsurface static and dynamic data sets working closely with engineers and other subsurface disciplines to identify value-generating opportunities
• Assist in framing and prioritizing technical service work.
• Supervise and verify sedimentological, reservoir quality, and integrated geology studies undertaken in the SedStrat specialist team, and as appropriate, those undertaken in assets.
• Provide input into management presentations and reports.
• Provide carbonate sedimentology and reservoir quality coaching and mentoring in areas of developed expertise across bp.
• Develop and maintain deep carbonate sedimentological and diagenetic skills across a range of reservoir types through reading, attending consortia workshops and external conferences.
• Quickly develop a strong technical reputation as a bp subject matter expert, and where appropriate, publish high quality innovative technical work internally and externally e.g. at industry-wide conferences and formal manuscript publications.
• Assist/lead teaching and development of bp courses with significant carbonate geological content.
• Act as a focal point for carbonate-focused JIPs/consortia, ensuring that maximum value is gained from them.
EDUCATION:
Minimum requirement MSc Geology degree level; preferably PhD level or equivalent experience.
EXPERIENCE AND JOB REQUIREMENTS:
• A deep understanding of carbonate sedimentary rocks across a range of depositional settings (e.g. platform, ramp, reefal, slope, basinal, lacustrine). In particular, the successful candidate will be able to demonstrate a strong understanding of carbonate facies analysis, depositional architecture, diagenesis, reservoir quality evolution, high-resolution sequence stratigraphy, and stratigraphic frameworks.
• An ability to scope and co-ordinate reservoir description and characterization projects, some involving external contractors, to deliver high-quality products that can be practically applied to subsurface problems.
• Experience in carbonate reservoir management/production, and at least one of the following: exploration, appraisal, early field development.
• An ability to describe carbonate core and outcrops independently, to a high standard, integrating sedimentology, textures, diagenesis, fractures, and reservoir quality observations.
• Ability to organize and lead geologic integrated field trips and core workshops, particularly focused on carbonate systems and reservoir analogues.
• Strong communication skills (written and verbal). Experienced with presenting to senior management to influence both vertically and horizontally in the organization.
• Ability to context switch while supporting more than one team at pace with the ability to pragmatically right-scope products.
• Managing carbonate analogues databases and contributing to reservoir quality benchmarking efforts.
AN ABILITY TO:
• Generate multiple depositional, diagenetic, and stratigraphic scenarios
• Use static and dynamic fluid data to test, improve and rank those models
• Describe subsurface uncertainty and risks and their impact on profile and resource delivery
• Skillfully correlate wireline logs, integrate reservoir data (e.g. core, seismic and image logs), dynamic data (sat logs, PLTs, PBU etc) and generate multiple geological models.
• A good understanding of, and ability to integrate with, other subsurface subject areas (Petrophysics, Geophysics, Reservoir Engineering)
DESIRABLE:
• A minimum of 10 years’ broad geological experience, ideally gained through work assignments in different areas and basins, dominantly within carbonate systems.
• Experience working in multi-discipline/multi-function project teams and ability to influence others to provide quality inputs to ensure quality team delivery.
• Ability to organize and lead cross-team workshops and meetings.
